_readme: Hand-authored weekly grid for the CBS station in /otr Station mode (station.js). Same rules as abc.grid.json:
listener's local clock, composite week (each slot is a real CBS day and time from one season, neighbours may differ),
conf: verified = printed in a season ratings table (Jim Ramsburg, GOld Time Radio); likely = standard reference knowledge;
approx = day confirmed by the catalog's episode dates, hour placed by judgment; fill = a labelled stand-in.
CBS Radio Mystery Theater (1974-82) is far outside the composite's era but it is CBS, and it fills the late hour every night.
name: CBS
tagline: What CBS was carrying at this hour, this day of the week, 1938-56
blurb: A composite week of the Columbia Broadcasting System: Jack Benny, Amos 'n' Andy, Edgar Bergen and Red Skelton on Sunday night after the 1948 talent raids; Lux Radio Theatre on Monday at 9; Mystery Theater, Mr. and Mrs. North and Life with Luigi on Tuesday; Dr. Christian, Groucho, Bing Crosby and Burns and Allen on Wednesday; Suspense and Casey, Crime Photographer on Thursday; Hopalong Cassidy and Gang Busters on Saturday; Beulah at 7 every weeknight and the CBS Radio Mystery Theater late every night. Episodes run back to back with no commercials, so a half hour slot often fits two. Your local clock, like an affiliate.

slots.src: Arthur Godfrey Time, CBS weekday mornings 1945-72 (NYT logs 9 and 11 Nov 1948: WCBS 10:30 'Arthur Godfrey Show'; Chicago Tribune 8 Nov 1948: WBBM 9:30 CT); a handful of broadcasts survive, daytime fill takes over when they run out
Ma Perkins, CBS weekdays 1:15 PM, 1942-60 (NYT log 11 Nov 1948: WCBS 1:15; Chicago Tribune 8 Nov 1948: WBBM 12:15 CT; Oxydol)
Perry Mason, CBS weekdays 2:15 PM, 1943-55 (NYT log 8 Nov 1948: WCBS 2:15; Chicago Tribune: WBBM 1:15 CT; episode dates confirm Mon-Fri)

slots.label: Lowell Thomas and the News (fill)
slots.src: Lowell Thomas moved his 6:45 newscast to CBS in 1947 and kept it until 1976 (NYT logs 8-12 Nov 1948 and 6-10 Nov 1950: WCBS 6:45); no usable recordings, quarter-hour strips fill
Beulah, CBS weekdays 7:00 PM, 1947-54 (ratings tables: M-F 7:00 15 CBS; NYT logs Nov 1948, Nov 1950, 3 Nov 1952: WCBS 7:00)

slots.label: Jack Smith Show (fill)
slots.src: Jack Smith sang the CBS 7:15 quarter hour for Procter and Gamble 1945-52 (NYT logs Nov 1948 and Nov 1950: WCBS 7:15); strips fill

slots.label: Club 15 (fill)
slots.src: Club 15 with Bob Crosby held CBS 7:30 weeknights 1947-53 (NYT logs 11 Nov 1948, 6-10 Nov 1950, 3 Nov 1952: WCBS 7:30); not on archive.org, strips fill
Blondie, CBS Monday 7:30 PM, 1943-44 (ratings table: Mon 7:30 30 CBS); Sundays 7:30 1946-48

Inner Sanctum Mysteries, CBS Monday 8:00 PM, 1946-50 (ratings tables: Mon 8:00 30 CBS; NYT log 8 Nov 1948: 'Inner Sanctum: Front Page Murder'; episode dates confirm Mondays); ABC Monday 8:00 by the fall of 1950

Burns and Allen, CBS Wednesday 10:00 PM, 1949-50 (ratings table: Wed 10:00 30 CBS; 1950 episode dates confirm Wednesdays)

The Aldrich Family, CBS Friday 8:00 PM, 1945-46 (ratings table: Fri 8:00 30 CBS); the NBC years' shows play

The Adventures of Philip Marlowe, CBS 1950 (episode dates: Fridays, Tuesdays and Wednesdays); Friday 9:00 placed. Sunday 8:30 in the fall of 1948 (Chicago Tribune 7 Nov 1948: WBBM 7:30 CT)

slots.src: Let's Pretend held CBS Saturday 11:05 AM, 1934-54 (NYT log 13 Nov 1948: WCBS 11:05), with Junior Miss at 11:30; not harvested, Saturday serials fill

slots.label: CBS Radio Mystery Theater
slots.src: CBS Radio Mystery Theater ran nightly 1974-82, by far the latest thing on this dial; most affiliates carried it late in the evening, 10:30 placed
Lum and Abner, CBS weekdays 5:45 PM, 1947-48 (NYT log 4 and 5 Nov 1947: WCBS 5:45 'Lum 'n' Abner-Sketch'); a Sunday 10:00 half hour by the fall of 1948
